dialogue.text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. I see you're experiencing some hand tremors and memory issues; when did you first start noticing these symptoms?
It started about a year ago with a little shaking in my left hand, but it's been getting worse lately. My wife also had to take over the bills because I've been getting quite forgetful.
I'm sorry to hear that. Does the shaking in your hand occur mostly when it's resting in your lap, or when you're reaching for something?
It’s mostly when I’m just sitting here with my hands in my lap. Once I start reaching for my book or trying to do something, it usually seems to settle down a bit.
That's a helpful observation. Have you noticed any stiffness in your limbs or that you are moving more slowly than you used to?
I have noticed that I'm moving a bit slower, and my wife says I don't seem to show much expression on my face lately. My voice has also become quite soft, making it harder for people to hear me.

Have you experienced any unusual visions, like seeing things that aren't there, or noticed any changes in your sleep, such as acting out your dreams? I'd also like to perform a physical examination to check your muscle tone.

Have you had any trouble with your balance or suffered any recent falls, and do you feel lightheaded when you stand up quickly? I would also like to order some imaging to get a clearer picture of what is happening.

I haven't had any trouble with my balance or felt dizzy when I stand up. Now that you mention it, though, I have noticed that I can't smell things like my morning coffee or flowers as well as I used to.

Are you taking any medications for nausea or mood, and is there any family history of similar tremors or neurological conditions? Also, have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits, such as constipation

I only take my aspirin and amlodipine for my blood pressure, nothing for nausea or my mood. My mother had schizophrenia, but I don't recall anyone in the family having shakes like these. As for my stomach, everything has been regular and I haven't noticed any constipation.

Yes, my handwriting has become quite small and cramped, almost like I'm running out of room on the page. It’s become very difficult for me to even sign my name clearly anymore.

I have noticed that my steps are much shorter and I tend to shuffle along the floor more than I used to. Sometimes I feel like my feet are stuck for a second when I first try to get up from my chair to start walking.

It is a relief to hear there might be an explanation for why I’ve been feeling so slowed down. Does this mean there is something that can help me get back to paying my bills and speaking clearly again? My wife is worried that my memory will only continue to get worse.

I appreciate you being thorough, Doctor. I'm ready to start whatever treatment you think is best so I can stop shuffling and hopefully get some of my steadiness back.
